meta.name: Resolve ecommerce order exceptions with Anthropic Claude and Slack

parameters.content:
## AI Order Exception Agent — Policy-Constrained Autonomous Resolution

This is an agent that takes real, controlled ACTIONS, not just text. It listens for order exceptions (payment failed, address undeliverable, inventory shortage, fraud-score flagged, carrier delay) from your OMS, gathers order + customer + inventory context, asks Claude to decide the correct resolution action from a strict allow-list of tool calls, and then actually executes that action through real APIs — with every action re-validated in deterministic code against policy limits (max refund/credit amount, fraud hard-stop) before it's allowed to run.

### How it works
1. Webhook - New Order Exception receives the exception event from your OMS (also testable via Manual Trigger + Set - Sample Exception Payload)
2. Set - Config centralizes API URLs and policy limits: maxAutoRefundAmount, maxAutoCreditAmount, requireHumanApprovalAboveAmount, slackEscalationChannelId
3. Three parallel HTTP Request nodes fetch order details, customer profile/history, and inventory/substitute SKUs; Merge - Combine Order Context joins them into one item
4. HTTP Request - Claude: Decide Resolution Action sends that context and forces Claude to choose exactly ONE action from a fixed allow-list (reissue_payment_link, substitute_sku, reroute_carrier, issue_store_credit, refund_order, escalate_to_human) plus the parameters that action needs and its reasoning
5. JS - Parse & Validate Decision parses that safely AND re-validates it against policy — amount ceilings, the fraud-flag hard-stop, and any unknown/disallowed action name all get force-overridden to escalate_to_human. The AI proposes; deterministic code disposes
6. JS - Log Decision (Pre-Execution) writes the decision to the audit trail BEFORE anything runs, so it's on record even if execution fails
7. Switch - Route To Action Executor dispatches to exactly one narrow-scoped API call per allowed action — Claude never gets raw API/database access, only this pre-built menu
8. JS - Merge Execution Result + JS - Log Decision (Post-Execution) record what actually happened against the original decision, completing the audit trail
9. HTTP Request - Notify Customer Of Resolution sends the customer-facing update; escalated cases skip this until a human acts

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: OMS/order platform API, payment processor API, inventory API, carrier/shipping API, Anthropic API (header auth, x-api-key), Slack API, Google Sheets or DB for the audit log
3. Edit Set - Config: maxAutoRefundAmount, maxAutoCreditAmount, requireHumanApprovalAboveAmount, slackEscalationChannelId, and every API URL
4. Activate the workflow, or use the Manual Trigger with the sample exception payload to test end to end

### Requirements
- Order/OMS platform API access (read order, write status)
- Payment processor API access (refund, re-charge, payment link)
- Inventory API access (stock levels, substitute SKUs)
- Carrier/shipping API access (reroute, re-schedule)
- Anthropic API access (Claude)
- Slack API access (human escalation + notifications)
- A sheet/DB to append the action audit log (this workflow uses Google Sheets as an example — swap for your DB)

### How to customize
- Add more resolution tools to the allow-list (e.g. partial refund, expedite shipping) as your policy allows
- Tighten or loosen requireHumanApprovalAboveAmount and the fraud-flag hard-stop
- Add a post-action verification step (e.g. confirm refund actually posted) before marking the case resolved
- Feed the audit log back into future prompts so Claude's action choices improve with real outcome data

## 1. Trigger & Context Gathering

- **Webhook - New Order Exception** — receives the exception event from your OMS (also works via Manual Trigger + Set - Sample Exception Payload for testing).
- **Set - Config** — centralizes API URLs, policy limits (max auto-refund/credit amounts, human-approval threshold), and the Slack escalation channel.
- **HTTP Request - Fetch Order Details** — pulls the order record the exception applies to.
- **HTTP Request - Fetch Customer Profile & History** — pulls the customer's profile and order/support history for context.
- **HTTP Request - Fetch Inventory & Substitute SKUs** — pulls current stock levels and any substitute SKUs, in case the exception is inventory-related.
- **Merge - Combine Order Context** — joins all three into one item so the agent gets a single, complete picture.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - AI Decision (Constrained Tool Choice)

parameters.content:
## 2. AI Decision — Constrained to an Allow-List of Actions

- **HTTP Request - Claude: Decide Resolution Action** — sends the exception type, order, customer history, and inventory context, and forces Claude to choose exactly ONE action from a fixed allow-list (reissue_payment_link, substitute_sku, reroute_carrier, issue_store_credit, refund_order, escalate_to_human) plus the parameters that action needs and its reasoning — never free-form text.
- **JS - Parse & Validate Decision** — parses that safely AND re-validates it in code against policy: amount ceilings, fraud-flag hard-stop, and unknown/disallowed action names all get force-overridden to escalate_to_human. The AI proposes; deterministic code disposes — this is the actual safety control, not the prompt.

## 3. Controlled Action Execution

- **JS - Log Decision (Pre-Execution)** — writes the decision to the audit trail BEFORE anything runs — so even if execution fails or the workflow crashes, the intended action is on record.
- **Switch - Route To Action Executor** — dispatches to exactly one real, narrow-scoped API call per allowed action:
  - HTTP Request - Execute: Reissue Payment Link
  - HTTP Request - Execute: Substitute SKU
  - HTTP Request - Execute: Reroute Carrier
  - HTTP Request - Execute: Issue Store Credit
  - HTTP Request - Execute: Refund Order
  - Slack - Escalate To Human (the only non-API branch — a real person decides)
- Each execution node only has permission to do its one named action — Claude never gets raw API/database access, only this pre-built menu.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Post-Execution Logging & Customer Notice

parameters.content:
## 4. Post-Execution Logging & Customer Notification

- **JS - Merge Execution Result** — all five automated-action branches converge here; records what actually happened (success/failure, provider response) against the original decision.
- **JS - Log Decision (Post-Execution)** — appends the outcome to the same audit trail row/record as the pre-execution log, so every case has a full before/after trail — proposed action, policy checks applied, and real-world result.
- **IF - Skip Notification For Escalations** — branches on whether the case was auto-resolved or escalated:
  - Automated action → **HTTP Request - Notify Customer Of Resolution** (order platform's own notification/email endpoint)
  - Escalated → **Set - Case Closed No Customer Notice (Escalated)** — no customer notice sent until a human acts

assignments.value: ={{ { orderId: 'ORD-88213', exceptionType: 'payment_failed', exceptionTimestamp: new Date().toISOString(), customerId: 'CUST-55210', orderTotal: 84.50, currency: 'USD', fraudScoreFlagged: false } }}

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Fetch Customer Profile & History
HTTP Request - Fetch Inventory & Substitute SKUs
HTTP Request - Claude: Decide Resolution Action

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 1000, system: "You are an order-exception resolution agent. You MUST choose exactly one action from this fixed allow-list: reissue_payment_link, substitute_sku, reroute_carrier, issue_store_credit, refund_order, escalate_to_human. Never invent a different action. Respond with ONLY a JSON object: { action: one of the allow-list values, actionParams: object (fields depend on action - e.g. refund_order needs amount and reason; substitute_sku needs substituteSkuId; reroute_carrier needs newAddressId or serviceLevel; issue_store_credit needs amount and reason; reissue_payment_link needs nothing extra; escalate_to_human needs escalationReason), confidencePercent: number, reasoning: string }. If the order is fraud-flagged, or the situation is ambiguous, or no listed action clearly fits, choose escalate_to_human.", messages: [ { role: "user", content: JSON.stringify({ exceptionType: $json.exceptionType, orderId: $json.orderId, orderTotal: $json.orderTotal, currency: $json.currency, fraudScoreFlagged: $json.fraudScoreFlagged, orderDetails: $json.orderDetails, customerProfile: $json.customerProfile, inventoryOptions: $json.inventoryOptions }, null, 2) } ] }) }}

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Execute: Reissue Payment Link

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ newAddressId: $json.actionParams.newAddressId || null, serviceLevel: $json.actionParams.serviceLevel || null, reason: $json.reasoning }) }}

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Execute: Issue Store Credit

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ orderId: $json.orderId, customerId: $json.customerProfile.id, amount: $json.actionParams.amount, currency: $json.currency, reason: $json.actionParams.reason || $json.reasoning }) }}

nodes.name: HTTP Request - Notify Customer Of Resolution

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: 'email', message: 'Your order ' + $json.orderId + ' exception (' + $json.exceptionType + ') was resolved: ' + $json.action.replace(/_/g, ' ') + '.' }) }}
